Field guide 35

Access Control Litestone has two orthogonal access control systems: row-level policies (@@allow/@@deny) and level-based GatePlugin. Aggregation Returns a single object of computed values across all matching rows. Audit Logging Litestone provides field-level and model-level audit logging via the logger database driver. CLI Reference bunx litestone <command> [flags] Edge fields — `@edge` / `@scoped` Attach a field value to a relationship instead of a row. Encryption Litestone provides field-level protection at rest. File Storage The FileStorage plugin stores file bytes in S3-compatible object storage (Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, AWS S3, MinIO) or local… Filtering // Equality Full-String Search Litestone builds FTS5 virtual tables and sync triggers automatically. Getting Started bun add @frontierjs/litestone Gotchas Production surprises and things that behave differently than you'd expect. Typed JSON columns A type is a reusable shape for JSON values. JSON Schema output generateJsonSchema(schema, options) turns a parsed .lite schema into one JSON Migrations Litestone uses two migration modes: autoMigrate for development (like prisma db push) and file-based migrations for production… Multi-Database A single Litestone schema can route models to multiple SQLite databases, append-only JSONL log files, and auto-schema audit… Multi-Tenancy One declaration, in the seed. A tenancy { } block at the top of onQuery — Production Query Logging onQuery gives you visibility into every SQL query Litestone executes. Litestone Performance Audit 1 open Date: 2026-07-18 · Version audited: @frontierjs/litestone 1.0.6 · Runtime: Bun 1.3.13 (Linux x64) Performance Litestone is designed for SQLite's single-writer, multi-reader model. Publishing Notes on publishing @frontierjs/litestone to npm. Querying // Return all matching rows Relations model Account { Replication Litestone wraps Litestream for continuous WAL replication to S3-compatible storage. Roadmap What's coming, what's being considered, and what's known to need fixing. Schema Schemas live in .lite files. Syntax is close to Prisma's SDL with SQLite-native extensions. Sequences @sequence provides per-scope auto-increment — a counter that restarts for each unique value of a scope field. Soft Delete Add @@softDelete to a model and Litestone handles all the details: filtering, restore, cascades, and partial indexes. Sorting An orderBy key must be something SQLite can put in an ORDER BY: a stored Litestone Studio — Feature Review & Roadmap Recommendations Date: 2026-07-18 · Reviewed: src/tools/studio.html (4,417 lines) + the Studio server in src/tools/cli.js Studio Studio is Litestone's browser UI. Testing Litestone ships a /testing subpath with everything needed for fast, deterministic test suites: in-memory clients, factories,… Traits A trait is a reusable model fragment — a chunk of fields and model-level attributes that get spliced into a model via @@trait(T). TypeScript Litestone is written in JavaScript but ships full TypeScript support via generated declarations. Why Litestone There are good ORMs already. Here's why you'd choose Litestone specifically. Window Functions Window functions add computed columns to each row based on a surrounding set of rows (the "window").

The surface, as its README groups it 45

Why In most stacks, your data model is described in five places — an ORM schema, a validator library, TypeScript types, middleware for access control,… How it compares The comparison is organized around what you can declare in the schema and what derives from those declarations. Quick start bunx litestone init # create schema.lite + litestone.config.js Schema Schemas live in a .lite file. Syntax is close to Prisma's SDL with SQLite-native additions. Multi-database Route models to separate SQLite files, JSONL logs, or auto-schema audit loggers: Multi-tenancy Declared in the seed, one block, two strategies. @@external — querying tables Litestone doesn't own @@external marks a model whose table is managed outside Litestone — a SQLite view, an FTS5 virtual table, a table created by a migration tool, or a… createClient import { createClient } from '@frontierjs/litestone' Row-level policies @@allow and @@deny compile to SQL WHERE injections — filtering happens in SQLite, not JS: Access control — GatePlugin Level-based access control. Assign levels 0–9, declare required levels per operation: @system and @guarded — two halves of one grid Only one of the two touches reads: @@transitions — a state machine at the Data boundary An enum field whose legal moves are declared, enforced on every write, and @version — optimistic concurrency model Order { @@scope — a named predicate a caller can ask for The policy compiler, made explicit and opt-in: @derived — a value SQLite computes, so you can filter and sort by it model Task { @@hasTemplates — definition versus instance A category most apps grow by hand: rows that are a definition sitting in the Encryption model User { Query API db.user.findMany({ where, orderBy, limit, offset, include, select, withDeleted,… onQuery — production query logging const db = await createClient({ path: './schema.lite', The audit trail — @@log records a write, $audit records an event @@log(audit) covers writes, which means the events an application most Write events — $tapEvents Every write announces, and the event says whether it can name its row: Is this a valid filter? — $checkWhere / $checkOrderBy A layer above needs to grade a caller-supplied where or orderBy before Migrations import { create, apply, status, verify, autoMigrate } from '@frontierjs/litestone' Schema functions Reusable named SQL expressions — define once, use on any model: @sequence — per-scope auto-increment model Quote { @from — derived relation fields Computed aggregates and lookups from related models — evaluated at query time, not stored. aggregate() and groupBy() // Simple aggregate Recursive tree queries Self-referential models (a field referencing the same model) automatically support CTE-based tree traversal: Window functions Window functions add computed columns to each row based on a set of surrounding rows — rankings, running totals, moving averages, period comparisons. query() — unified dispatcher Routes a single args object to findMany, groupBy, or aggregate based on its shape. Scopes Reusable named query fragments registered per model. JS migrations Migrations can be .js files alongside SQL files in the migrations directory: Computed fields // computed.js File storage — FileStorage plugin import { FileStorage, fileUrl, fileUrls, useStorage } from '@frontierjs/litestone' ExternalRefPlugin — custom external-backed fields FileStorage is built on ExternalRefPlugin, a base class for any field whose value is stored outside SQLite. Testing utilities Litestone is the Testing realm's Data half. SQLite utilities // Hot backup — safe during writes Studio bunx litestone studio # → http://localhost:5001 Shipping a schema change A schema change is a deploy question before it is a migration, and CLI reference litestone init scaffold schema.lite + litestone.config.js Standalone binary The CLI compiles to a single executable with bun build --compile. Single-file library build Separately from the CLI binary, the library bundles to one file. Multi-file schemas // schema.lite Litestream Litestone sets the pragmas Litestream requires (WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busytimeout=5000). Convention decisions

Field guide 1

Junction — Architecture Junction-internal design notes. Verified against the tree on 2026-08-01.

One document per capability, in packages/junction/docs/.

The surface, as its README groups it 35

Quick start Working on Junction itself, from a clone of the monorepo: Where Junction lives in an app A FrontierJS app puts one directory at the root per realm, and Junction owns api/: Structure The package itself: The REPL The fastest way to explore a running API. The secret sauce This is the most important file in the codebase. Response helpers ctx.json(data, status?) Health and metrics import { healthPlugin } from '@frontierjs/junction' Middleware import { cors, helmet, rateLimit, requestLogger, correlationId, csrf } from… CSRF protection The bearer token pattern (Authorization: Bearer ...) is inherently CSRF-safe — a cross-origin page cannot set arbitrary request headers, so it can… Circuit breaker import { circuitBreaker } from '@frontierjs/junction' API versioning const app = createApp({ Idempotency-Key A mutating request carrying an Idempotency-Key header executes once. Bulk operations Bulk patch and remove without an id are disabled by default — a guard against accidental whole-table mutations: Config options Auth import { createBetterAuthAdapter, createBetterAuthPlugin } from '@frontierjs/junction' Running as somebody ctx.auth.user propagates, so a service call made inside a request already runs Schema validation import { createSchema, v } from '@frontierjs/junction' Service caching Add cache: true to any service to automatically cache find and get responses. Database const app = createApp({ config, migrations: './migrations' }) Litestone ORM Litestone is Junction's first-party SQLite ORM. Transactions Multi-step operations that need atomicity — create a user and a workspace together, or not at all — require a transaction. File uploads Junction handles multipart file uploads transparently. Testing import { createTestApp, testCtx, request, callService } from '@frontierjs/junction' OpenAPI app.configure(openapi({ Webhooks At-least-once webhook delivery built on the existing event bus. Scheduler app.scheduler.every('5 minutes', async () => { /* cleanup */ }) Workers Bun threads for CPU work that would otherwise block the event loop. Browser client @frontierjs/junction/client is a zero-dependency browser client for connecting Sierra/Mesa frontends (or any browser app) to a Junction API. Email Junction ships a built-in email plugin with two independent tiers. What is actually mounted The HTTP surface is emergent: services auto-mount, plugins register their own, Tier 1 Plugins First-party plugins built specifically for Junction. Interface-first adapters The blast radius of swapping a provider is exactly one file. Scripts Deploying bun run build:app <entry> (also junction build <entry>) turns an app into a deployable artifact. Dependencies Runtime: bun >= 1.0.0

The idea The system is two halves, equally weighted. Three kinds of class Only two of the three compose freely. Tones A tone is one variable. Seven of them, and they work on everything that Themes One class on any ancestor. They nest, because it is all custom-property Overriding it Everything ships inside a cascade layer, and unlayered CSS beats every Using it with UnoCSS Uno is not required, but running it alongside is supported (ruled What's in the box Frame app shell topbar sidebar screen pane view Syntax highlighting Code blocks are highlighted by glow() in @frontierjs/toolbelt, Icons The package ships no icons — it sizes what it finds. The focus ring Every focusable thing in the package rings the same way, from one rule in State comes from the platform Where a state is one the browser or a screen reader already knows about, the Behaviour is not included Visual treatment is a class; keyboard, focus and ARIA management are a Browser support Chrome 119+ · Safari 16.4+ · Firefox 128+ Status Alpha, and honest about it: zero production consumers so far. Rulings 106

2026-08-16 FJS-D06 the coherence-review vocabulary, ruled. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-15 FJS-D03 Context is a per-realm concept. It is plural, it is documented, and it is not unified. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-15 FJS-D19 Litestone's Plugin gets a name. The concept is NOT renamed. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-15 FJS-D02 a custom service method is a METHOD. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-13 FJS-D29 the process a fleet server runs is an OUTPOST, and infrastructure gets place nouns while AI gets personified ones. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-08 A resource file is named for its noun — PascalCase, singular — one Resource per file. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-09 A pagination control is .pagination-link, not .page. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-06 The email component kit is @frontierjs/email-kit. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-01 Model names are PascalCase and singular, always. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-01 Named gate syntax is canonical; digits are the compact form. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-06 Signal and Event are two words for two things, both legal. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-06 Policy keeps exactly one meaning, and it is not "business rule". Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-06 Projection is adopted for a read model only. Naming & vocabulary
2026-08-16 FJS-D05 tenancy is DECLARED in the seed, one block, two strategies; row tenancy compiles to @@deny and never to @@allow. Access control
2026-08-15 FJS-D22 a column says the system writes this with @system, and the application fills it by naming the column on the write. Access control
2026-08-14 The identity ladder: @@gate("8") is for credential material, not for User. Access control
2026-08-10 Basecamp's gate ladder: a level is a fact about a caller IN A WORKSPACE, so it is resolved per request and carried on the principal. Access control
2026-08-10 A tier above every tenant is a SEPARATE service, and the bit that grants it is a column named for the standing it grants. Access control
2026-08-10 A status column that nothing reads is not a state, and suspension needs a door on each side. Access control
2026-08-10 A machine account is created from an admin screen. Access control
2026-08-06 Raw SQL is available through asSystem() only, on any schema that declares access rules. Access control
2026-08-01 Gates enforce by default when declared; undeclared imposes nothing. Access control
2026-08-17 FJS-D27 Litestone has atomic update operators, and the COLUMN decides one is an operator at all (FJS-D27). Query & write semantics (Litestone)
2026-08-16 A write announcement has two shapes, and the write says which (FJS-307). Query & write semantics (Litestone)
2026-08-16 FJS-D34 announce is per CALL, with a client-level floor (FJS-D34). Query & write semantics (Litestone)
2026-08-01 Unknown where fields: WARN on reads, ERROR on writes. Query & write semantics (Litestone)
2026-08-01 Unknown data keys are silently stripped. Query & write semantics (Litestone)
2026-08-01 take/skip are rejected with a pointer to limit/offset. Query & write semantics (Litestone)
2026-08-01 Missing required fields on create are a ValidationError. Query & write semantics (Litestone)
2026-08-01 @@strict model flag: PARKED. Query & write semantics (Litestone)

CI phases 10

01 hygieneEverything here is about the difference between THIS working copy and a fresh clone.fast
02 structureThe architecture rules, run over this repo's own apps and packages with the same engine `fli check` gives a client app.fast
03 snapshotsA snapshot is a generated artefact committed beside its source, so a change nothing else in the repo can see arrives as a diff: the access rules enforced below the API, the DDL every hand-written statement binds to, the JSON Schema three packages validate…fast
04 accessWhat did this branch do to who may do what.fast
05 coverageSkipped is not passed. The aggregate `--filter '*'` walks straight past a package with no `test` script and prints nothing at all about it.fast
06 registryScaffolds an app, packs the working tree into it, installs and builds it.fast
07 scaffoldfast
08 typecheckTwo halves: the direction of the ratchet (a git question) and the count itself (each package's own script already answers that, and exits 1 above its ceiling).fast
09 deploy`fli new` → `fli make:deploy` → `fli deploy:local`: does the deploy pipeline containerise a real app? ~30s and it needs a Docker daemon, so it sits in the full tier rather than the pre-push one.full run
10 testsSequential on purpose: several suites bind ports and start real servers, and interleaved output from four different runners is unreadable when one fails.full run

bun run buildbun run cibun run ci:fastbun run hooks:installbun run testbun run typecheck

Invariants, and what checks them 19

1 Dependency directionLitestone ← Junction ← Sierra, never reverse.attention only
2 Model names are PascalCase singular(model Lead → db.lead); @@external exempt.model-name-case model-name-plural
3 App layoutdb/ at the root and each SURFACE a directory beside it: api/, web/, widgets/ (embeddable scripts) and extension/ (a jetty browser extension).app-layout
4 One owner per translation.Exactly one place turns a thrown value into an HTTP status, one wraps/unwraps the result envelope, one parses $-params into ctx.directives, one announces a mutation, one startup phase list…attention only
5 One owner per app.<thing>.Claim it with app.claim(name, value); type it by augmenting an exported interface, never by redeclaring the property — declaration merging requires identical types, so a redeclaration…attention only
6 Access is declared in the schema, not in hooks.Gates, @encrypted, @guarded, @@transitions are enforced at the Data boundary.attention only
7 Protected fields are redacted in the audit trail.@encrypted/@guarded/@secret log as [redacted] in field entries and in before/after snapshots.attention only
8 Caller-supplied names never enter a SQL pattern.attention only
9 Patch semantics: an explicit null clears.Test key presence (key in updates), not ??.attention only
10 $ is transport syntax only.ctx.query is filters, ctx.directives is {limit, offset, orderBy, select}; nothing past the bridge sees a $.attention only
11 The nearest delegation root owns an event.Roots nest; a handler must fire once.attention only
12 Mesa compiler output is reproduciblescope ids are content-addressed, which is what makes CSS dedupe work across the two compilers a static build runs.attention only
13 @frontierjs/css is the styling language.Style with a tone (danger) and a treatment (outlined), never a colour.attention only
14 Typecheck baselines ratchet down only.scripts/typecheck-baselines.json, one number per package; absent means 0.attention only
15 A clean compile is not proof of valid JS.Compiler tests parse their output.attention only
16 Runnable examples are verified, not sketches.A broken one is a bug.attention only
17 Four markdown files at a package root is the standardREADME.md, CLAUDE.md, PROJECTSTATE.md, CHANGES.md; everything else in <pkg>/docs/.package-root-md
18 In a Sierra app, src/resources/ holds .mesa files.A Resource is a UI-realm noun, written in the UI-realm language.resource-dir-mesa resource-script
19 A resource file is named for its noun — PascalCase, singular — one Resource per file.App.mesa exporting export const apps; the same split the Data realm makes between model App and db.app.resource-file-name resource-one-per-file widget-entry-name

14 of 19 are held up by nothing a machine runs — fli check covers 5. 2 more rule(s) guard a live hazard rather than an invariant. Rules are packages/cli/core/checks.js, run over this repo by the structure CI phase and over a client app by fli check.
